gloss: to creep up; to steal near

definitions.gloss: to creep up; to steal near; to sneak up on
definitions.explanation: To approach quietly and stealthily, so as not to be noticed. Used both literally (a person sneaking up) and figuratively (danger, old age, or fear approaching gradually).

examples.japanese: {猫|ねこ}が{獲物|えもの}に{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る。
examples.english: The cat creeps up on its prey.

examples.japanese: {背後|はいご}から{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る{足音|あしおと}が{聞|き}こえた。
examples.english: I heard footsteps sneaking up from behind.

examples.japanese: {不安|ふあん}が{静|しず}かに{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}ってくるのを{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I felt anxiety quietly creeping up on me.

notes:
USAGE:
Literally used for people or animals sneaking up on someone. Figuratively, it is commonly used with abstract subjects like {危険|きけん} (danger), {老|お}い (old age), {不安|ふあん} (anxiety), or {影|かげ} (shadow) to describe something approaching ominously and gradually.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {背後|はいご}から{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る (to sneak up from behind)
- {危険|きけん}が{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る (danger creeps up)
- {老|お}いが{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る (old age creeps up)
- そっと{忍|しの}び{寄|よ}る (to creep up quietly)

CONJUGATION:
Godan verb (る→ら行): {忍|しの}び{寄|よ}らない, {忍|しの}び{寄|よ}ります, {忍|しの}び{寄|よ}って
